title: Internal-Cover Characterization of Universal-Branch Shielding
scope: Any finite CNF local formula F_C(X_C,B_C) with a finite internal variable set C and boundary variable set B_C.

definitions.internal_projection_of_clause: I_D(X_C) = OR of exactly those literals of D whose variables lie in C; the empty disjunction is FALSE.
definitions.internal_cover: U_C(X_C) = AND_{D in C_C} I_D(X_C); the empty conjunction is TRUE.
definitions.residual_branch: For a total internal assignment alpha:C->{0,1}, R_alpha(B_C)=F_C(alpha,B_C) after exact Boolean simplification.
definitions.kappa_C: If R_C is identically TRUE, kappa_C=min{|A|: A is a subset of internal assignments and OR_{alpha in A} R_alpha is identically TRUE}; otherwise kappa_C=INFINITY.

theorem.statement: U_C is satisfiable iff there exists an internal assignment alpha such that R_alpha(B_C) is identically TRUE iff kappa_C=1.
theorem.corollary: U_C satisfiable implies R_C is identically TRUE.
theorem.nonconverse_warning: R_C identically TRUE does not imply U_C satisfiable in general; multiple non-universal residual branches may jointly cover the boundary cube (distributed shielding).

forward: Assume U_C is satisfiable and let alpha satisfy U_C.
For every local clause D, alpha satisfies at least one literal of D whose variable lies in C, because alpha satisfies I_D.
Therefore each D is already TRUE after substituting alpha, independently of all boundary-variable values.
Hence F_C(alpha,B_C)=TRUE for every B_C, so R_alpha is identically TRUE.
Therefore a one-element set {alpha} covers the full boundary relation and kappa_C=1.
reverse: Assume there exists alpha such that R_alpha(B_C) is identically TRUE.

Fix any local clause D. If alpha satisfied no internal literal of D, then after substituting alpha the residual of D would contain only boundary literals and could not be identically TRUE as a non-tautological CNF clause under all boundary assignments.
Therefore alpha satisfies at least one internal literal in every D.
Thus alpha satisfies every I_D and hence satisfies U_C.
kappa_equivalence: By definition kappa_C=1 exactly when one residual branch R_alpha alone is identically TRUE.
Combining this definition with the forward and reverse directions yields U_C in SAT iff exists alpha:R_alpha=TRUE iff kappa_C=1.

mechanistic_classes.UNIVERSAL_BRANCH_SHIELDING: U_C in SAT; equivalently kappa_C=1; necessarily R_C=TRUE.
mechanistic_classes.NO_UNIVERSAL_BRANCH: U_C in UNSAT; equivalently no single R_alpha is TRUE.
mechanistic_classes.DISTRIBUTED_SHIELDING: U_C in UNSAT and R_C=TRUE, so kappa_C>1.
mechanistic_classes.SEMANTIC_SIGNAL: R_C is neither TRUE nor FALSE.
